subject: research/osrobot-weedsrc
professional: a precision-agriculture robotics researcher who works on laser and site-specific weed control and reviews field-robot throughput studies. They would check first whether the detection rates are what the papers report and under what conditions, whether a speed law can be read off two different robots, whether the modelled treatment throughput matches the robots the rates came from, and whether the kill numbers are more than the closed form 1-(1-p*k)^n

evidence.correctness: Ran `PYTHONPATH=src python3 experiments/run.py` (4.2 s): byte-identical to the committed experiments/results.txt. Independently recomputed in my own script (scratchpad weedsrc/recompute.py, run with python3 -I, no import of the subject): (1) the log-linear fit through (0.2, 0.8894) and (0.425, 0.862) gives p_max 0.9145, v_blur 7.190 m/s, matching the README's 0.914 / 7.19; rates at 1/2/4 km/h 0.880/0.846/0.784 (B) and 0.609/0.530/0.402 (A) match exactly. (2) Closed-form kill for independent passes, (1-h)*(1-(1-0.992*p)^n): B 1 km/h 1 pass 0.873 (sim 0.875), 4 km/h 2 passes 0.950 (sim 0.952), 2 km/h 1/2/3 passes 0.840/0.974/0.996 (sim 0.842/0.976/0.996), hidden 10% 3 passes 0.896 (sim 0.897); my own 200,000-weed Monte Carlo gives 0.9504 and 0.8732. The +0.002 offset is sampling noise: the subject's own model over 200 other seeds gives 0.8393 for the 0.842 row. (3) Drive-time bound for one pass at 1 km/h (15 lanes x 60 m, 20% mud at half speed, 4 s turns) ~67.5 min vs 68.4. (4) The source values themselves were checked against the papers' abstracts (Crossref for doi 10.3389/fpls.2022.1017803: 88.94% at 0.2 m/s; arXiv API for 2512.10319: 86.2% at 42.5 cm/s): both correct. Every headline number is right for the model as written; no error bars are reported.
evidence.completeness: README claims checked end to end: 6 tests (6 run, OK), run.py regenerates results.txt (identical, ~4 s against 'about 5 s'), figure.py reads sweep 1 from results.txt and writes kill_vs_time.svg (via research/_shared/linefig), the A rows reproduce osrobot-weedpass (0.778 kill, 71.8 min for 2 passes at 2 km/h: research/osrobot-weedpass/experiments/results.txt line 49), all three sweeps present. Next steps are listed as not done. Live page https://marisstella.app/research/osrobot-weedsrc/ loads (HTTP 200) with the same headline numbers. Nothing claimed as done is missing.
evidence.verification: `PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v`: 6 tests OK in 0.06 s. Five seeded mutations in src/osrobot_weedsrc/model.py, only one caught: dropping the laser-queue term on the on-the-move path (line 206), ignoring the hidden share (line 111), inverting the treatment success test on the on-the-move path so a treatment kills 0.8% instead of 99.2% (line 203), and halving the blur rate in p_detect (line 93) all leave every test green; only flipping the sign in fit_detector (line 89) fails 2 tests. The tests check the fit and monotonicity (better detector or more passes kill more) but nothing checks a kill share against the closed form, the on-the-move time, or the hidden share, which are exactly what the headline rests on. test_fit_values asserts v_blur 7.17 +/- 0.05 against an exact 7.190.
evidence.craft: Read src/osrobot_weedsrc/model.py (217 lines), tests/test_model.py, experiments/run.py, experiments/figure.py. The model is copied whole from osrobot-weedpass (stated), so run_inline (line 129) and run_scout (line 148) and the energy constants are carried but unused by any experiment. The fitted detector is applied by run.py mutating the module global M.V_BLUR (run.py:32, 38) while the module defaults (V_BLUR=2.0, p_max=0.7) remain detector A, so p_detect(p_max, v) silently depends on whoever last set the global; the module docstring says the speed law is fitted, but calling the module as shipped gives detector A's law. hidden_share draws from the same rng as detection, so 'random draws shared across rows' holds for fields but not for detection draws in sweep 2. Small, readable, standard library only; no input validation is needed for a research script.
evidence.claims: Checked against results.txt and my reruns: headline 0.952 in 39.8 min vs 0.875 in 68.4 min (pass); fitted rates 0.880/0.846/0.784 (pass); one pass 0.875/0.842/0.781 in 68.4/34.7/20.8 min (pass); +0.134 for 37 min, third pass +0.020 (pass); hidden rows 0.842..0.594 and 0.996..0.700 (pass); 10% hidden third pass +0.019 (pass); density times 34.1/34.7/61.4 (pass); density gains '+0.133, +0.134, +0.134' (partial: results.txt rows give 0.134/0.134/0.134, unrounded 0.1335/0.1341/0.1330); A rows reproduce weedpass (pass); 6 tests, ~5 s (pass); both source values (pass, now confirmed from abstracts; the README's 'read from snippets, not opened' caveat is honest). Limits are stated plainly (two robots, extrapolation to 4 km/h, independence, perfect tracking, no validation). 'The ranking ... gets stronger' is supported (gap 0.031 under A, 0.077 under B). One stated limit understates a source fact: the arXiv robot's own abstract reports 87 s of operating time per metre at that 86.2% detection rate, which the 'time savings are an upper bound' caveat does not convey.
evidence.fitness: Nearest prior work: static and moving laser-weeding robot studies (Mathiassen et al. 2006, Biosystems Engineering, laser dose per weed; Xiong et al. 2017, Computers and Electronics in Agriculture, laser-weeding robot with path planning and time per weed), the two cited detection papers, and commercial on-the-move laser weeders (Carbon Robotics LaserWeeder) and the EU WeLASER project, plus the repeated-pass literature on mechanical weed control. None of the robot or multi-pass literature is cited; the only baseline is the sibling project's assumed detector. With independent detections the kill share is the closed form 1-(1-0.992p)^n (my recomputation matches every row within 0.003), so the simulation's contribution is the time accounting under on-the-move treatment. The useful, honest finding is that correlated misses (the swept hidden share) cap multi-pass gains, but that share is unsourced and swept. A researcher could build on the code and the sourced detection points, but the result is a sensitivity re-run of a toy model, not a new finding about laser weeding.
evidence.domain: Against field-robotics practice: (a) the 'speed law' is a two-point fit across two different robots, crops, cameras and detectors (YOLOX in corn on a tracked platform at 0.2 m/s; a six-wheeled robot at its 'optimal' 0.425 m/s), so the 2.7-point difference is not a speed effect; the README says the points come from two robots but the headline still extrapolates the fitted law to 4 km/h. 'Optimal speed' in the arXiv abstract suggests detection there is not monotone in speed. (b) The time axis assumes the beam treats every weed while driving at up to 4 km/h with a 0.73 s dwell, but the robot that supplies the 86.2% reports 87 s per metre of operating time, and the Frontiers robot aims a 5-DOF arm; neither source robot treats on the move, so the detection rates are paired with a throughput no source robot achieved. (c) Detection rate is per-weed recall here; the papers' definitions were not read. The Frontiers paper also reports an 85% weed dry-weight control efficacy that could have served as a validation point. The laser-safety note (IEC 60825-1) is correct practice.

defects.what: The on-the-move kill and time path that produces every headline number is untested: inverting the treatment success test (kill 0.8% per treatment), removing the laser-queue time term, or ignoring the hidden share all leave the 6 tests green; no test compares a kill share with the closed form 1-(1-0.992p)^n

The detection 'speed law' is fitted across two different robots, crops and detectors (one speed each), so the 2.7-point difference is confounded with platform, and the fit is then extrapolated to 4 km/h for the headline; the arXiv source calls 42.5 cm/s its optimal speed, which suggests detection is not monotone in speed there

The time axis assumes on-the-move treatment at 1 to 4 km/h with a 0.73 s dwell, but the robot supplying the 86.2% detection rate reports 87 s of operating time per metre and the other robot aims a 5-DOF arm; the detection rates are paired with a throughput neither source achieved, and the stated limit ('time savings are an upper bound') does not say how far

No laser-weeding robot or multi-pass weed-control prior work is cited (e.g. Mathiassen et al. 2006; Xiong et al. 2017; on-the-move commercial laser weeders), and with independent detections the kill share is a closed form, which the README does not say

Fitted detector applied by mutating the module global M.V_BLUR from run.py while the module defaults stay detector A's (V_BLUR 2.0, p_max 0.7); importing the model as shipped gives the assumed law, contrary to the module docstring
Copied model carries unused run_inline and run_scout and unused energy terms
Density gains quoted as +0.133, +0.134, +0.134; results.txt rows give +0.134, +0.134, +0.134 (unrounded 0.1335, 0.1341, 0.1330)
test_fit_values expects v_blur 7.17 +/- 0.05 while the fit is exactly 7.190; the tolerance would admit a wrong fit
No seed spread or interval is reported; the 20-seed rows sit about +0.002 above the closed form (sampling noise, 200 seeds give 0.8393 for the 0.842 row), the same size as some quoted differences

verdict: Every number in results.txt reproduces byte-for-byte, the two-point fit (p_max 0.9145, v_blur 7.190 m/s) and every kill share agree with an independent closed form and Monte Carlo within 0.003 (sampling noise), and both source detection rates are confirmed against the papers' abstracts; the README states its limits honestly. It misses the bar on verification and on the median: only 1 of 5 seeded mutations is caught, and the on-the-move path that produces all headline numbers can be made to kill 0.8% per treatment with all 6 tests green. For a precision-agriculture robotics reviewer the method is weak: the 'speed law' is a slope between two different robots extrapolated to 4 km/h, the robot behind the 86.2% figure reports 87 s per metre while the model treats on the move at up to 4 km/h, and no laser-weeding prior work is cited. The durable point, that correlated (hidden) misses cap what extra passes buy, is sound but rests on a swept, unsourced share.
